infoText: Base64 encoding increases file size by approximately 33%. Large PDFs may take longer to process.
detailed_description: The PDF to Base64 tool converts binary PDF documents into Base64-encoded ASCII strings, enabling efficient transmission of binary data through systems designed for text handling. Base64 encoding maps 8-bit binary data to 6-bit ASCII characters using a 64-character alphabet (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '+', '/'), with padding ('=') to align data lengths. Users often require this conversion when embedding PDFs directly into JSON payloads, XML documents, or HTML data URLs, where binary content would otherwise corrupt formatting. For example, attaching a PDF to an SMTP email (which traditionally handles ASCII) or storing a PDF signature in a database field restricted to text requires Base64 encoding. The tool processes files client-side via JavaScript FileReader API, parsing PDF headers (e.g., %PDF-1.7) and binary streams, then applying Base64 encoding without intermediate server transfers. This ensures sensitive documents remain private. Technical considerations include MIME type preservation (application/pdf) and handling PDF cross-reference tables during encoding. Output strings can exceed the original file size by ~33%, a tradeoff for text compatibility.
usage_steps: Click 'Choose File' to select a PDF from your device (max size 50MB).
Toggle 'Preserve MIME Header' to include 'data:application/pdf;base64,' prefix for data URLs.
Click 'Convert' to initiate client-side Base64 encoding via Web Worker thread.
Review encoded output in the text area, which auto-copies to clipboard on completion.
Use 'Download Result' to save the Base64 string as a .txt file for integration into code.
Optionally verify integrity by re-decoding with browser DevTools console (atob(BASE64_STRING)).
usage_examples: Embedding a 10KB invoice PDF into a JSON API request body for a document management system.
Creating a data URL for a PDF brochure to inline in a single-file HTML email template.
Transmitting a digitally signed PDF through a legacy EDI system that only accepts ASCII characters.
Storing a PDF thumbnail preview inside an SQLite database's TEXT column for an offline app.
